head: 4d64d2364961ad14abb24d8144d7a41750d36307
summary: Only fflib_Objects.cls changed. Iteration 2 drove nearly all the real gain: Limit headroom went from 58.3 to 97.5 because each call now builds one lookup set instead of scanning the list for every value. Iterations 4-5 raised Code coverage (90.5 to 97.3) only by merging untested null checks into one helper, not by adding tests. Resource efficiency barely moved (80.5 to 81.1, fflib_SObjectDomainTest fell 81.4 to 80.2). Two behaviours changed with no test to catch them: matching now depends on hashCode() as well as equals(), and an empty input against a null objects list now throws instead of returning true.

behaviourChanges.title: Membership now uses Set hashing (hashCode+equals) instead of List.contains (equals only)
behaviourChanges.detail: Baseline checked membership with getObjects()?.contains(value), which uses equals(). Evolved builds Set<Object> members from getObjects() and calls members.contains(), which uses hashCode() first. Any user class whose equals() is overridden without a matching hashCode() can now return false for a value that is present, which flips containsAll to false and containsNot to true. In this repo fflib_QueryFactory overrides equals with no hashCode. SObjects, primitives and classes using identity equality are unaffected.
behaviourChanges.evidence: fflib_Objects.cls:88, fflib_Objects.cls:91; fflib_QueryFactory.cls:179; baseline containsAll(Set)/containsNot(Set) loops
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Define a test inner class with equals() comparing a field but no hashCode override. Build a Domain with instance a1, then call containsAll(new List<Object>{a2}) and containsNot(new List<Object>{a2}), where a2.equals(a1). Assert that the result matches contains(a2).

behaviourChanges.title: Null objects list with an empty values collection now throws
behaviourChanges.detail: If a subclass calls setObjects(null), the baseline returned true for containsAll(empty) and containsNot(empty) because the loop never ran. Evolved runs new Set<Object>(getObjects()) before the loop and throws NullPointerException. Non-empty values already threw in the baseline (! on null Boolean), so only the empty-input case changed. isEmpty() checking for null shows a null list is expected.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Test subclass that calls setObjects(null). Assert containsAll(new Set<Object>()) and containsNot(new List<Object>()) return true (baseline behaviour), or decide to make throwing the specified behaviour.

behaviourChanges.title: Every call now builds a set the size of the collection and no longer stops early
behaviourChanges.detail: Each containsAll/containsNot call builds a set of every domain member, even when values is empty or has one item. The baseline could return after one partial scan when the first value missed. This is a large win for bulk inputs but slightly slower for tiny inputs on large domains. It also adds heap per call, and hashing SObjects costs CPU proportional to their populated fields. Heap use could matter with collections of tens of thousands of records called repeatedly in one transaction.
behaviourChanges.proposedTest: Headroom test: a domain of about 10k SObjects with fields populated, calling containsAll on a single-element list in a loop. Assert that Limits.getHeapSize() and Limits.getCpuTime() stay within a budget.

patterns.title: Build the lookup set once per call instead of scanning the list per value
patterns.detail: This is the correct fix for the O(n*m) cost and gave the only large score gain. It quietly changes equality to depend on hashCode, so the contract should be documented or tested.

patterns.title: Boolean flag parameter merging containsAll and containsNot logic
patterns.detail: allMatch(values, expectMember) with null returning !expectMember is compact but obscure. Readers must work out that containsNot means 'all values absent' and that null maps to the opposite of the flag. It was done mainly to remove one uncovered line (coverage-driven dedup).

patterns.title: Removing null checks to raise coverage instead of testing them
patterns.detail: Iterations 4-5 raised coverage by deleting duplicated untested null-check lines, not by adding tests. Behaviour was kept, but the null contract is still unverified (line 86 is uncovered).

patterns.title: Manual Iterator loop over Iterable<Object>
patterns.detail: This lets List and Set overloads share a single helper without copying. Iteration 3 found no CPU gain over the copy, and the result is more verbose than a for-each loop.

testGaps.title: Null values argument
testGaps.detail: No test passes null to containsAll or containsNot. The false/true null results are unverified, and line 86 is the only uncovered line.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert containsAll((List<Object>) null) == false, containsAll((Set<Object>) null) == false, containsNot((List<Object>) null) == true, containsNot((Set<Object>) null) == true.

testGaps.title: Empty values collection
testGaps.detail: The fact that an empty input always gives true for both containsAll and containsNot is not tested.
testGaps.proposedTest: Assert containsAll(new List<Object>()) and containsNot(new Set<Object>()) are both true on a non-empty domain and on an empty domain.

testGaps.title: Classes with equals() but no hashCode()
testGaps.detail: The change from List.contains to Set.contains is not covered.
testGaps.proposedTest: See the first behaviour change: an inner class with equals() only, asserting containsAll agrees with contains().

testGaps.title: Null objects list via setObjects(null)
testGaps.detail: Nothing tests what happens when the collection itself is null.
testGaps.proposedTest: Subclass calling setObjects(null). Pin the expected result (true or a specific exception) for empty and non-empty inputs to containsAll and containsNot.

testGaps.title: Null elements and duplicates inside values
testGaps.detail: Null elements inside the values collection, and duplicate values in a List, are not tested.
testGaps.proposedTest: Domain containing null: containsAll(new List<Object>{null}) == true. Domain without null: containsNot(new List<Object>{null, null}) == true.

other.title: Limit headroom rests on one synthetic test
other.detail: The headroom score comes from one test, headroomBulkContainment. The jump to 97.5 is real for that workload, but it does not test heap use at volume or single-value calls on large domains.

other.title: Resource efficiency barely changed
other.detail: fflib_SObjectsTest rose 79.6 to 82 and fflib_SObjectDomainTest fell 81.4 to 80.2. These classes do little containment work, so the changes are noise. Iteration 8 confirmed that removing the dead initializer at fflib_Objects.cls:32-34 is also below noise.

other.title: Unrelated small cleanups left out
other.detail: isEmpty() calls getObjects() twice and size() is not null-safe while isEmpty() is (fflib_Objects.cls:99, 109). These are untouched and harmless, but inconsistent.
